decision: Do not infer mainland broad-ETF timing from individual A/H premium findings: the same empirical paper reports insignificant aggregate-index terms. This rejects the proposed transfer as currently unsupported, not all possible A/H mechanisms.
method_distinctions: Issuer-specific A/H relative prices are distinct from ETF price/NAV premiums and index-level timing.
The retained HSI methodology is September2017 version1.2; it defines a ratio of weighted sums with FX conversion, not an arithmetic average of issuer premiums.
HSI dissemination while either market is open does not certify simultaneous executable prices.
The publisher's AH Smart cheaper-share-class selection is a different strategy from buying a mainland broad ETF.
The analyst-reaction paper supports persistent segmentation, not a costed aggregate ETF signal.
remaining_requirements_for_a_materially_: Distinct economic justification at the investable ETF or disclosed-holdings level, with explicit exposure to the already read findings.
Point-in-time membership, weights, FX, publication clock, historical versions and practical account-cost feasibility.
Predeclared rule and independent validation evidence; no threshold or sign search justified by this source review.
next: Preserve this narrow source-only closure and continue review of a distinct mechanism. Do not download A/H history solely to tune an unsupported broad-ETF timing transfer.
